notes_on_text: The chapters have only numbers. The entries of the contents give each chapter a title of the editor’s, made of a few of the topics the printed contents lists for it, in its own words; the full lists are in the printed contents, which is kept in the JSON.

The front matter is numbered as if it had eight pages before the contents, but this copy has only four (half-title, title page, and dedication); nothing seems to be lost. The author’s preface to a later London edition says that the first edition had no preface and a map, later removed; if the map stood in this edition, it is not in this copy.
Decorated initial letters, head-pieces, and tail-pieces are shown small. The pictures that the print sets with the text running round them stand between paragraphs, near where they are printed.
summary: Ménie Muriel Dowie, a young British woman, spent a summer travelling alone in the eastern Carpathians of Galicia, then a province of Austria-Hungary and now part of Ukraine; the book does not give the year. She stayed for some weeks at a farm at Mikuliczyn, bathing, riding, and wearing peasant sandals, and then rode on through the mountains with local guides, lodging with the priest’s family at Kosmacz and with peasants at Źabie, sleeping out of doors, trying a timber raft, and coming back by way of Kossów, Kołomyja, and Cracow.

She writes about the Hucul people, their dress, work, and customs, the Jews of Galicia, the Polish language, and her reasons for travelling alone. The book has many pen drawings of people and things she saw.
